text:
anna: FYI we're seeing a recurring tail-latency pattern on shelf-7 (usw1-edge) that lines up with heavy host-batched jobs + MIG slices. Not classic NIC/PCIe; NVLink and HBM cross-traffic looks like the vector.

reza: can you share the perf dump?

anna: pasted sampling from 03:22 UTC:

```
perf_sample shelf-7/node4
nvlink_retries=88, nvlink_err=1, hbm_bw=72GB/s, hbm_p95=89GB/s
mig_partitions=[/gpu0:4g,/gpu1:2g,/gpu2:6g,/gpu3:4g]
host_batch_qdepth=54
```

anna: spikes start during batch warmup windows and sustain for ~10-15m.

kai: interesting. Are the heavy batches pinned to host-accelerated lanes (node-local batch runner)?

anna: yes - host-batched runner packs lots of small synchronous jobs. Tenant ids: t-spark (batch), t-voice (low-latency slices), t-mlflow (background).

reza: if host batches are saturating NVLink between GPUs, MIG slices sharing the same NVSwitch get slowed. Could be exacerbated by mixed NVLink gens in the shelf.

ops-bot: auto-detect rule matched: nvlink_retry_rate > 75 in 10m for shelf-7 -> flagged.

kai: immediate mitigations: 1) evict host-batched pods from shelf-7 for 20m, 2) move low-latency slices to hotlanes, 3) throttle host-batched concurrent jobs via quota. Which is least risky?

anna: throttle host-batched concurrency first; it's reversible and less churn. We should also mark shelf-7 as "nvlink_hot" to influence allocator.

reza: agree. Add a short-lived placement policy: "nvlink_hot -> avoid_batch". Implement in allocator as a soft-avoid with weight 0.1 so we don't starve other racks.

kai: can we add a per-tenant noisy-count metric so billing/product can see candidates for isolation?

billing-bot: created metric: tenant_isolation_score. Linking to billing dashboard: https://billing.internal/isolations?t=tenant

ops-bot: placement policy patch queued: branch "nvlink_avoid_weighted". CI run started.

anna: I ran a local sim: imposing soft-avoid reduces real-time p95 by ~32% on affected shelf, batch throughput drops 9%. Seems acceptable.

reza: long-term options to list in doc: rack-level hard isolation for latency-sensitive tenants (costly), stricter dedicated carveouts per HW-gen, or smarter NVLink-aware packing in allocator (account for nvlink bisection bandwidth in scoring).

kai: add to triage: audit racks for mixed NVLink firmware or switch gen mismatches. Those shelves should be flagged as fragile.

anna: inventory quick check shows shelf-7 has 2 nodes on nvlink-fw v1.1 while rest are v1.3. I'll open an infra ticket to schedule firmware drift remediation.

reesa: (typo for reza) can we also expose per-host NVLink egress counters to tenant owners so they understand noisy behavior?

billing-bot: exposure request created: owners will see a weekly digest with noisy events and cost delta.

ops-bot: canary rollout results (after soft-avoid flip at 03:40 UTC): realtime p95 from 260ms -> 160ms on shelf-7, batch throughput -7%. No allocator failures observed.

sre-oncall: propose alert: shelf_nvlink_retry_rate > 60 (5m) -> P2 page. This would've caught earlier.

anna: agreed; add that to playbook and tag nodes with hw-gen so allocator scoring can prefer homogeneous racks.

kai: also let's prototype a tiny experiment: 1-day trial of moving one noisy tenant to a fractional dedicated carveout and measure cost delta vs SLO improvements. If uplift is clear, hand to sales/CS as upsell.

reza: I'll draft the experiment plan + metrics (p95, throughput, tenant_isolation_score) and share by EOD.

anna: owners: reza (experiment plan + audit), kai (allocator soft-avoid change), ops-bot (canary annotations), billing-bot (dashboard digest). Recheck tomorrow standup.

anna: thanks all ":rocket:"
